title: How Water Moves in Plants
seo_title: Year 3 Science: How Water Moves in Plants Worksheets (Celery and Coloured Water)
standard_text: Investigate the way in which water is transported within plants.
meta_desc: Free Year 3 science worksheets on how water moves in plants: roots, stems and leaves, the celery and coloured water investigation, wilting and evaporation. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Roots, up the stem, to the leaves.
key_sub: Tiny tubes in the stem carry water up from the roots.
body_html:
How to think about it

Water travels up a plant: from the soil, into the roots, up the stem, to the leaves and flowers.

  • The stem has tiny tubes, like straws, that carry water upwards.
  • Celery or a white flower in coloured water shows where the water goes.
  • Most water leaves through the leaves into the air. A plant without enough water wilts.
Example

Celery in blue water. Where does blue appear?

Water goes up the stem

Answer: in the leaves at the top

Example

After the roots, where does water go?

Up the tubes

Answer: the stem

Common mistakes

  • Thinking leaves take in water from the air.
  • Thinking water goes down from the leaves to the roots.
  • Thinking a wilted plant is always dead.

faq.q: How does water get into a plant?
faq.a: The roots take in water from the soil. It then travels up tiny tubes in the stem to the leaves and flowers.

faq.q: What does the celery investigation show?
faq.a: When celery stands in coloured water, the colour travels up the stem to the leaves. This shows that water moves up through the stem.
When there is not enough water in the stem and leaves, they cannot stay firm, so they droop. Watering the soil usually helps them stand up again.

items.q: Why does a plant in a sunny window need watering more often than one in a shady corner?
c: More water evaporates from its leaves.

items.q: Water moves through a plant. Where does it go after the roots?
items.e: Soil → roots → stem → leaves and flowers → out into the air.

items.q: Water moves through a plant. Which does the water pass through first: the soil or the roots?
c: Water does not pass through either.
They happen at the same time.
items.e: Soil → roots → stem → leaves and flowers → out into the air.
